input.question: Why can retrieval-augmented models still be swayed by poisoned documents even when they detect them, and how does the number of poisoned documents matter?

supporting.quote: reasoning reduces Cordon Rate from 0.205 to 0.075 and Leakage Rate from 0.235 to 0.140
supporting.why: Detected poison can still steer answers; reasoning reduces that.

supporting.quote: poisondetection rates decrease from 25% (50/200) in the minority condition to 10% (20/200) in the majority condition
supporting.why: A majority of poisoned documents lowers detection.

supporting.quote: is not driven by a single dominant poisoned passage, but by the accumulation of weak adversarial signals across retrieved sources
supporting.why: Many weak poisoned documents add up.

draft_answer: Detecting poison doesn't stop it from shaping answers, though reasoning reduces this; when poisoned documents are the majority, detection drops; and distributed attacks work by accumulating many weak poisoned signals.
